en: to fast; to go without food

examples.ko: 그는 다이어트를 하려고 이틀 동안 단식해요.
examples.en: He fasts for two days to diet.

examples.ko: 단식하는 동안에도 물은 충분히 마셔야 해요.
examples.en: Even while fasting, you need to drink enough water.

examples.ko: 친구가 일주일 동안 단식하고 몸이 많이 약해졌어요.
examples.en: My friend fasted for a week and became very weak.

examples.ko: 며칠씩 단식하면 위험할 수 있다고 의사가 말했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said fasting for several days at a time can be dangerous.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 주말에 하루만 단식할 거예요.
examples.en: I will fast for just one day this weekend.

examples.ko: 단식하던 사람들이 오늘 아침에 죽을 먹기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The people who had been fasting started eating porridge this morning.

explain: 굶다는 먹을 게 없거나 못 먹어서 안 먹는 것이고, 단식하다는 건강이나 항의 같은 이유로 일부러 안 먹는 거예요. 병원 검사 전이나 종교 때문에 안 먹을 때는 '금식하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 검사 전에는 여덟 시간 금식해야 해요.
phrases.en: You have to fast for eight hours before the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 검사나 종교 때문에 안 먹을 때는 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often for fasting before a medical test or for religion.

phrases.en: He went on a hunger strike to protest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주장을 알리려고 일부러 굶는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to deliberately not eating to make a point.

phrases.example: 하루 동안 단식해 봤는데 많이 힘들었어요.
phrases.en: I tried fasting for a day, and it was really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여 경험해 본 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -아/어 보다 to talk about trying it as an experience.

explain_en: Voluntary fasting — diet, health, protest, hunger strike. 굶다 is going without food because you have none or cannot eat; 단식하다 is fasting on purpose, for health or as a protest. Before a medical test or for religious reasons, Koreans more often say 금식하다.

t90.ax: He fasts for two days to diet.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에는 소고기 등심을 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: Tonight we're grilling and eating beef sirloin.
Sirloin is a little fattier than tenderloin.
I made pork cutlet with pork loin.
Two servings of sirloin here, please.

examples.ko: 등심 스테이크는 중간 정도로 익혀 주세요.
examples.en: Please cook the sirloin steak medium.
Sirloin was on sale at the mart, so I bought a lot.

explain: 소나 돼지의 등 쪽 고기예요. 식당에서는 '안심', '갈비'와 함께 부위 이름으로 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: I made pork cutlets with pork loin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소고기뿐 아니라 돼지고기 부위 이름으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for beef but also as a pork cut name.

phrases.en: It was our anniversary, so we went for sirloin steak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서양식 구이 메뉴 이름에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the names of Western-style grilled dishes.

phrases.en: I bought a geun of sirloin at the butcher shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 살 때 무게 단위 '근'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the weight unit 근 when buying meat.

explain_en: It is meat from the back of a cow or pig. In restaurants you often hear it alongside other cut names such as '안심' and '갈비'.

examples.en: The museum preserves old bowls.

examples.ko: 우리는 숲을 보존하려고 쓰레기를 줍고 있어요.
examples.en: We are picking up trash to preserve the forest.

examples.ko: 할머니가 오래된 한복을 상자에 넣어 잘 보존하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother put the old hanbok in a box and preserved it well.

examples.ko: 음식을 오래 보존할 수 있는 방법이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a way to keep food for a long time?
Preserving nature is important to everyone.

examples.ko: 사진을 잘 보존해서 아이들에게 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I kept the photos in good condition and showed them to the kids.

explain: '보관하다'는 물건을 어디에 두는 일이고, '보존하다'는 상태가 변하지 않게 지키는 일이에요. 자연, 문화재, 전통, 자료에 자주 써요. '자연 보존'처럼 명사로도 많이 쓰고, 일상에서 물건을 챙길 때는 '보관하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My grandmother keeps her old photos well preserved.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘'을 붙여 상태를 변하지 않게 신경 써서 지킨다는 뜻을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '잘' shows that someone takes care to keep the condition unchanged.

phrases.example: 이 책은 보존 상태가 아주 좋아요.
phrases.en: This book is in very good condition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '보존'을 써서 물건이 얼마나 원래대로 남아 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '보존' is used to describe how well something is kept as original.

phrases.en: We must protect the beautiful nature.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보존하다'보다 쉬운 말이고 널리 지킨다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word with the broader meaning of protecting something.

explain_en: Active, keeping relics, records or food unchanged (옛날 그림) '보관하다' is about putting something somewhere; '보존하다' is about protecting it so its condition does not change. Common with nature, heritage, tradition and records. For everyday belongings, '보관하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: In summer I eat noodles in yeolmu kimchi broth.
My mother made the yeolmu kimchi herself.
The yeolmu kimchi has fermented nicely and tastes tangy.
Yeolmu kimchi goes well with barley rice.

examples.ko: 열무김치 국물이 시원해서 자꾸 마시게 돼요.
examples.en: The yeolmu kimchi broth is so refreshing that I keep drinking it.

examples.ko: 열무김치 한 통을 이웃에게 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: I shared a container of yeolmu kimchi with my neighbor.

explain: 어린 무인 열무로 담근 김치로 국물이 많은 편이고 여름에 즐겨 먹어요. 국수를 말거나 비빔밥에 넣어서 먹는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: On hot days, noodles with yeolmu kimchi are the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시원한 국물에 국수를 말아 먹는 여름 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A summer dish of noodles in cool kimchi broth.

phrases.en: For lunch I mixed and ate yeolmu kimchi bibimbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥에 열무김치를 넣고 비벼 먹는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rice mixed with yeolmu kimchi.

phrases.en: The yeolmu kimchi has ripened nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 김치가 먹기 좋게 발효되었을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when kimchi has fermented to a good taste.

explain_en: This is kimchi made from young radish, and it usually has a lot of broth and is a summer favorite. People often put it in noodles or in bibimbap.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 김치 제조법을 공개하지 않아요.
examples.en: This shop does not reveal its kimchi recipe.

examples.ko: 할머니는 비누 제조법에 대해 잘 아세요.
examples.en: Grandmother knows a lot about how to make soap.

examples.ko: 제조법이 간단해서 집에서도 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: The method is simple, so you can make it at home.

examples.ko: 이 치즈의 제조법은 아주 오래된 전통 방식이에요.
examples.en: The way this cheese is made is a very old traditional method.
After the method changed, the taste got better.
I looked up how to make natural cosmetics on the internet.

explain: 제조법은 공장이나 가게에서 물건을 만드는 방법이에요. 집에서 음식을 만들 때는 보통 '만드는 법', '요리법', '레시피'라고 해요. '비법'은 남이 모르는 특별한 방법이라서 제조법과 달라요.

phrases.en: I want to learn how to make bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 만드는 방법을 익힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when learning the method of making something.

phrases.en: This liquor is made with a traditional method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날부터 내려온 만드는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a way of making things handed down from long ago.

phrases.en: I looked up how to make soap at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 만들 때는 '제조법'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 제조법 when making something at home.

explain_en: 제조법 is the method for making a product in a factory or shop. For cooking at home people usually say '만드는 법', '요리법' or '레시피'. A '비법' is a special secret method that others don't know, so it is different.

examples.en: I put soybean oil in the pan and fried an egg.
I made jeon with soybean oil.
Soybean oil is cheap, so we use a lot of it.
Using soybean oil for frying tastes clean.
We ran out of soybean oil, so I went to the mart.
You can use soybean oil instead of olive oil.

explain: 콩으로 짠 기름이에요. 보통 집에서는 '식용유'라고 부르는 경우가 많아요. 고소한 향이 나는 '참기름'이나 '들기름'과는 쓰임이 달라서 볶음, 전, 튀김처럼 일반 요리에 써요.

phrases.en: We ran out of cooking oil, so I'm going to buy some.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리용 기름을 모두 가리키는 말로, 집에서는 보통 이렇게 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The general term for cooking oil, and what people usually say at home.

phrases.en: I coated the pan with soybean oil and stir-fried onions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팬에 기름을 얇게 펴 바를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for spreading a thin layer of oil in a pan.
phrases.en_equiv: to coat the pan with soybean oil

phrases.en: If you fry it in soybean oil, it gets crispy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 튀김 요리에 어떤 기름을 쓰는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which oil is used for frying.

explain_en: Soybean oil — mild cooking oil for frying. It is oil pressed from soybeans. At home people often just call cooking oil '식용유'. It differs from the aromatic '참기름' (sesame oil) and '들기름' (perilla oil) and is used for general cooking like stir-frying, jeon and frying.

examples.ko: 시장에서 활어를 사다가 회를 떠 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought live fish at the market and made sashimi from it.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 매일 아침 활어만 쓴대요.
examples.en: I heard this restaurant uses only live fish every morning.
The live fish are swimming energetically in the tank.
Sashimi from live fish is fresh and has a nice chewy texture.
A truck carrying live fish drove past.

examples.ko: 활어는 값이 비싸지만 맛이 훨씬 좋아요.
examples.en: Live fish is expensive, but it tastes much better.

explain: 횟집이나 수산시장에서 수족관에 있는 살아 있는 생선을 말해요. '활어회'처럼 회와 함께 자주 나오고, 냉동 생선과 구별할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I will eat live fish sashimi tonight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살아 있는 생선으로 만든 회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sashimi made from live fish.

phrases.en: There are many fresh live fish in the tank.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싱싱한'은 신선하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 싱싱한 means fresh.

phrases.example: 가게 아저씨가 활어를 바로 손질해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The shop owner prepared the live fish for me right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생선을 먹기 좋게 다듬을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning and preparing fish for eating.

explain_en: It refers to live fish kept in tanks at sashimi restaurants and fish markets. It often appears in '활어회' (live-fish sashimi) and is used to distinguish it from frozen fish.

examples.ko: 교통질서를 잘 지켜야 사고가 안 나요.
examples.en: You have to follow traffic rules well to avoid accidents.
They teach children about traffic rules in front of the school.

examples.ko: 모두가 교통질서를 지키면 길이 덜 막혀요.
examples.en: If everyone obeys traffic rules, the roads are less congested.
Traffic is so disorderly that walking feels scary.
They guide foreign tourists on traffic rules too.
A traffic order campaign was held this morning.

explain: 신호를 지키고 차선을 지키는 것처럼 길에서 모두가 따르는 약속을 말해요. '교통질서를 지키다'가 가장 자주 쓰이고, 어기면 '교통질서를 어지럽히다'라고 해요. '교통법규'는 법으로 정한 규칙이고, '교통질서'는 그 규칙을 지키는 길 위의 질서 상태를 말해요.

phrases.en: Jaywalking disrupts traffic order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속을 어겨서 길이 혼란스러워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when breaking the rules makes the road chaotic.

phrases.en: We received traffic safety education at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 지켜야 할 약속을 배우는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to learning the rules to follow on the road.

phrases.en: If you break traffic laws, you pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교통질서'보다 법으로 정한 규칙이라는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like rules set by law than '교통질서'.

explain_en: It means the shared rules everyone follows on the road, like obeying signals and lanes. The most common pairing is '교통질서를 지키다', and breaking them is '교통질서를 어지럽히다'. '교통법규' are the rules set by law, while '교통질서' is the orderly state on the road when those rules are followed.

examples.en: Is there a good restaurant around here?

examples.ko: 집 근방에는 큰 공원이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is one big park near my house.
The area around the school is very crowded every morning.
We decided to meet near the station.

examples.ko: 그 근방 길은 잘 몰라서 지도를 봤어요.
examples.en: I don't know the roads in that area, so I looked at a map.
I'm going to move to a city near Seoul.

explain: '근처'와 거의 같게 써요. '근방'은 '근처'보다 조금 글 같은 느낌이 있어요. '이 근방', '그 근방'처럼 '이/그/저' 뒤에 잘 붙어요.

phrases.en: There is a subway station near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근방'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Is there a pharmacy around here?
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 물을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when asking for directions.

phrases.en: I live near my company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 어디 가까이에 사는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 에, it tells where someone lives close to.

explain_en: Almost the same as '근처'. '근방' feels slightly more bookish. It pairs well with '이/그/저' as in '이 근방'.

examples.en: While hiking, I drank cool water at a spring.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 오래된 샘터에 모여 빨래를 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers gathered at the old spring and did their laundry.

examples.ko: 이 샘터는 물이 맑아서 사람들이 자주 찾아요.
examples.en: The water at this spring is clear, so people visit it often.
I rested for a moment on the bench next to the spring.

examples.ko: 샘터가 요즘 공사 중이라 물을 못 마셔요.
examples.en: The spring is under construction these days, so I can't drink the water.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 할머니와 샘터까지 물을 길러 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I walked with my grandmother to the spring to fetch water.

explain: 장식용으로 만든 '분수'와 달리, 땅에서 물이 솟는 곳이에요. 산이나 마을에 있는 곳을 말하고, '약수터'는 몸에 좋다고 알려진 물이 나오는 샘터를 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 우리 마을 샘터는 여름에도 물이 차가워요.
phrases.en: The spring in our village has cold water even in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마을 사람들이 함께 쓰는 샘터를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a spring that villagers share.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain and drank water at the spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'가 붙어 샘터가 행동이 일어나는 장소임을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에서', the spring is the place where the action happens.

phrases.en: The water at the spring is clear and cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샘터에서 나오는 물 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the water coming from the spring itself.

explain_en: Unlike '분수' (a decorative fountain), it is a place where water wells up from the ground, in the mountains or a village. '약수터' is a spring whose water is known to be good for the body.

t90.ax: While hiking, I drank cool water at a spring.

examples.en: While walking up the mountain path, I found a mineral spring.
My family exercises at the mineral spring every morning.
The water at the spring tastes cool and clean.

examples.ko: 아버지는 매일 물통을 들고 약수터에 가세요.
examples.en: My father goes to the spring every day with a water jug.
It takes about thirty minutes to walk to the spring.

examples.ko: 주말에는 약수터 앞에 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: On weekends, people line up in front of the spring.

explain: 주로 산이나 공원 근처에서 사람들이 물을 마시거나 떠 가는 곳이에요. 물 자체는 '약수'라고 하고, 장소는 '약수터'라고 해요. 어르신들이 산책과 운동을 겸해서 자주 가는 곳으로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I go to the mineral spring every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 장소로 가는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for going to that place.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to the mineral spring

phrases.en: The mineral spring water is cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소의 물을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the water from that place.

phrases.en: I drank mineral water at the spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '약수'는 물이고 '약수터'는 장소예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 약수 is the water and 약수터 is the place.

explain_en: It is a place near mountains or parks where people drink or collect spring water. The water itself is '약수', and the place is '약수터'. It often appears as a spot older people visit for a walk and exercise.

examples.en: I bought batteries at the neighborhood general store.
The general store has everything.
My grandfather runs a small general store.
The owner of the general store showed me the way.
The general store in front of the school closed down.

examples.ko: 잡화점으로 가는 길에 비가 오기 시작했어요.
examples.en: It started to rain on my way to the general store.

explain: 큰 마트나 다이소 같은 '생활용품점'과 비슷하지만, 잡화점은 동네의 작고 오래된 가게 느낌이 있어요. 요즘은 '문구점', '편의점'처럼 파는 물건에 따라 가게 이름을 더 많이 불러요.

phrases.en: There is a small general store at the end of the alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동네의 작은 가게 느낌을 살려 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Brings out the feel of a small neighborhood shop.

phrases.en: I went to the general store to buy thread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 물건을 사러 갈 때 써요. '-러 가다'와 함께 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when going to buy small items. Often paired with -러 가다.

phrases.en: The general store owner is very kind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게를 하는 사람을 말해요. '가게 주인'과 같은 구조예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who runs the shop. It has the same structure as 가게 주인.

explain_en: It is close to a '생활용품점' (household goods store) like a big mart or Daiso, but 잡화점 suggests a small, old neighborhood shop. Today people more often name shops by what they sell, such as 문구점 or 편의점.

examples.en: There is a ceramics exhibition room on the second floor of the museum.
You aren't allowed to take photos in the exhibition room.
Each exhibition room has a guide who explains the works.

examples.ko: 이 전시실은 조명이 어두워서 천천히 걸었어요.
examples.en: The lighting in this exhibition room was dim, so I walked slowly.

examples.ko: 새 작품을 놓으려고 전시실을 다시 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: They redecorated the exhibition room to place the new works.

examples.ko: 아이들이 전시실 앞에서 줄을 서서 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The children lined up and waited in front of the exhibition room.

explain: '전시관'은 건물 전체를, 전시실은 그 건물 안의 방 하나를 가리켜요. 박물관에서는 '제1전시실', '제2전시실'처럼 번호를 붙여서 구분해요.

phrases.en: Please look at the paintings in Exhibition Room 1 first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관에서 번호로 방을 구분할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in museums to tell rooms apart by number.

phrases.example: 특별 전시실에서는 새로운 작품을 보여 줘요.
phrases.en: The special exhibition room shows new works.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일반 전시와 따로 열리는 전시를 하는 방을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a room for exhibitions held separately from the regular ones.

phrases.example: 전시실 안에서는 음식을 먹을 수 없어요.
phrases.en: You can't eat food inside the exhibition room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전시실 내부의 규칙을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about rules inside the room.

explain_en: One room inside a museum or gallery (두 번째 전시실) '전시관' is a whole exhibition building, while 전시실 is a single room inside it. Museums number them, as in '제1전시실' and '제2전시실'.

examples.en: I sent my old car to the scrapyard.
I found a usable part at the scrapyard.
The car from the accident was moved to the scrapyard.
It's always dusty near the scrapyard.

examples.ko: 폐차장 직원이 차를 가지러 오기로 했어요.
examples.en: A scrapyard worker is coming to pick up the car.
Before going to the scrapyard, I checked the license plate first.

explain: 더 이상 못 타는 자동차를 처리하고 해체하는 곳이에요. 차를 없앨 때 '폐차하다'라고 하고, 그 일을 하는 곳이 폐차장이에요. 중고차를 파는 곳과는 달라요.

phrases.en: The car was badly broken, so I decided to scrap it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 폐차장은 장소이고, 폐차하다는 차를 없애는 행동이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 폐차장 is the place; 폐차하다 is the action of scrapping a car.

phrases.en: My uncle works at a junkyard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 곳을 말할 때 '에서'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 에서 marks the workplace.

explain_en: It is the place where cars that can no longer be driven are processed and dismantled. Getting rid of a car is '폐차하다', and this is where it happens. It is different from a used-car dealership.
